The width law and uniform block law both have mean zero, so Jensen gives both nonnegative deficits. The two linear sums eliminate the same slope and give the stated r_0 and block contributions. Adding the captured width T accounts for all exterior mass.

For each coefficient a_j, minimizing c_j a_j over its allowed scalar interval yields d_j min(0,a_j), independent of simultaneous realizability. Convex-order dominance makes the coefficients nonnegative by the hinge tests.

For the sufficient condition, the signed law difference is nonpositive on the block and nonnegative outside, and integrates every affine function to zero. Subtracting the secant from a convex function gives exactly the opposite inside/outside signs. If h=0, the centered law dominates the point mass by Jensen.
